messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty ALERT: service=canary-router severity=critical — error-rate > 5% for 3m, triggered at 1738501234. Pager: @emma_oncall.
pagerduty: auto-page fired -> P123456: Canary routing 503 spike (canary-router). Escalation policy: oncall -> sre -> eng.
emma_oncall: acked P123456 :wave: I'm on it, pulling logs and checking canary metrics. Any deploy in the last 30m? @olivia_releases
olivia_releases: deploying release/2026.03.15-canary two minutes before alert. Canary fraction 5%. Rolling out edge-proxy + router changes.
sandeep_sre: seeing high 503s on canary-router pods, p95 latency up. Metrics: backend-conns exhausted? Dumping pod logs.
emma_oncall: logs show repeated grpc: EOF and connection reset. Attaching sample: ```2026-03-15T03:20:12Z canary-router[abc123] ERROR connection reset by peer while proxying to model-backend-quant```
nate_platform: checking LB metrics — upstream health for canary backends fluctuating. A few pods have OOMKill in last 2m. Node memory pressure maybe.
olivia_releases: rollback flag? We can cut canary to 0% traffic. Rollout controller: redwoodctl rollout set canary-router --fraction=0. Runbook suggests traffic diversion first.
emma_oncall: doing diversion now. Command: ```redwoodctl traffic split canary-router --from=0.05 --to=0.0 --timeout=30s```
incident-bot: Command executed by @emma_oncall at 1738501335 — traffic fraction stepping to 0. Canary fraction now 0.00.
sandeep_sre: after divert, 503 rate dropped to baseline within 40s. p95 latency back to normal. Looks like issue confined to canary variant (new router build).
olivia_releases: confirmed canary variant has memory regression with quant kernel. Pinned to older image in CI we should revert. Will open rollback PR.
emma_oncall: P123456 update: mitigated customer-facing error by diverting canary -> incident severity reduced to major. Notifying CS. @cs_bot please run status page draft.
cs_bot: Draft status: "We experienced increased errors for a subset of requests routed to a canary release. Traffic was diverted and service restored. Engineers are investigating the release and users may see intermittent 503s between 03:20-03:24 UTC." Would you like to post? :eyes:
emma_oncall: Post now. Also tagging @sandeep_sre for postmortem. Add timeline + CI diff.
sandeep_sre: collecting diagnostics — attaching heap profiles and kernel logs. Noted OOM lines correlate with the quant kernel change in release/2026.03.15-canary. Will correlate memory usage from 03:15-03:25.
olivia_releases: opened rollback PR #342: revert router kernel patch. Will coordinate with eng to validate a canaryless rollback to stable image and then re-run canary with memory guardrails.
pagerduty: P123456 status -> acknowledged by @emma_oncall at 1738501250, mitigated at 1738501360, resolved at 1738501899 by @olivia_releases (post-rollout rollback merged).
emma_oncall: handoff summary for follow-up: root cause likely memory regression in quant kernel within router image — triggered OOMs in canary and exposed by spike. Mitigation: immediate traffic diversion, rollback PR merged, monitor for recurrence. Next steps: full postmortem with CI diff, add memory safety tests, add alert for canary pod OOMs.
olivia_releases: thanks team. I'll schedule the rollback verification run and coordinate a staged re-rollout after fixes. Marking the incident as resolved in PD and closing thread. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident P123456 marked resolved by @olivia_releases at 1738501899. Summary logged to incidents repo: /incidents/2026-03-15-canary-quant-memory-regression.md"
